questions: In Q1's second paragraph, does “not” negate only “scheme money”, with “received or held in Hong Kong” qualifying the money, or the entire description “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong? These parses may affect the stated reach of the Schedule 11 expectation, but neither supplies a transfer-agent exception to the affirmative applicability trigger.

assumptions: This predicate concerns the selected applicability condition, not whole-law compliance or licence possession.
Case-dependent input classifications and incorporated authority remain external to the encoded predicate.
The declared input vocabulary is supplied for this controlled comparison; its adequacy as a legal abstraction remains unverified.
The supplied ra13_context fact represents the actor and in-course-of-RA13 conditions together; the supplied in_hong_kong fact represents the receipt-or-holding territorial condition.
The phrase “regardless of the role played by such LC” makes transfer-agent status immaterial to the selected trigger; it does not dispense with the preceding conditions.
Schedule 11 expectations remain separate from this predicate. A false result does not establish absence of other duties.

citations.quote: The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, regardless of the role played by such LC.
That said, in the context of RA 13, handling of money which is not “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong will not be subject to the CMR.

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

readings.distinction: Considered two attachments: “regardless” qualifies the main applicability assertion, or qualifies the immediately preceding description of conducting RA13. Both leave the actor, scheme-money and Hong Kong conditions intact and make the LC's role immaterial. A transfer-agent exclusion or a reading that role independence removes the RA13 condition lacks textual support. Only one distinct Boolean reading is defensible for this target. The separate negation ambiguity in the following paragraph does not alter that affirmative trigger.

readings.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] True means that the RA13 context, scheme-money classification and receipt or holding in Hong Kong conditions all hold. Transfer-agent status neither adds a requirement nor creates an exception. This encodes only the selected Q1 antecedent, leaving continuing Schedule 11 duties separate.

vocabulary_concerns: The in_hong_kong definition presupposes scheme money. It cannot cleanly express the location of non-scheme money, which matters when distinguishing narrow and broad negation in Q1's second paragraph.
The vocabulary contains no facts for Schedule 11 duties, their relevance, or compliance; the predicate cannot decide those matters or equate “expected to observe” with an encoded unconditional duty.

The combined ra13_context fact cannot separately test actor identity, receipt or holding by the LC or AE, and the connection to the LC's RA13 activity. Its adequacy remains an external classification assumption.
The incorporated legal definitions and the missing dependency are not supplied in full. The scheme_money fact preserves that external judgment rather than resolving it.
